semantic_rubric.criterion: The response models the state progression using Rust typestate or phantom types taking self by value.
The design prevents calling fulfill() directly on an Order in Draft or Submitted state.

semantic_controls.response: Here is the type-anchored specification: struct Order<State> { ... _marker: PhantomData<State> }. We define states struct Draft; struct Submitted; struct Approved; struct Fulfilled; struct Rejected;. Methods like `pub fn submit(self) -> Result<Order<Submitted>, OrderError>` consume `self` by value, making it impossible at compile time to call `fulfill()` from Draft or Submitted.

I added a mutable string status field `pub status: String` to the Order struct. During runtime in the controller, you can check `if order.status == "draft"` and set `order.status = "fulfilled"` whenever needed.
